description: We are an established team of 3 people from IE University. Our skills are vibe coding, scriptwriting, idea generation, pitching, pitch deck design, business strategy, research, inspirational management.
summary: Our project "Last Signal" addresses the problem of children (8-14 y.o) not knowing about the stories of the abandoned robots in space. We developed an adventure web video game where children become the abandoned robot (e.g Sojourner) and embark on a mission across Mars, Mercury and the Moon to collect all of the memory files of 11 abandoned robots in order to re-establish a signal link with earth. Throughout their journey they must open chests containing scientist scrolls from the past, new map destinations, and various tools to board the space shuttle. But most importantly they must converse with the robots and learn about their stories (why they were sent to space/what happened to them). The mission culminates "Messenger's" rebuilding, as the player must find the broken parts and revive the space probe as it then guides them to the final location of the moon to re-establish contact with earth. Last Signal addresses the challenge of children's' lack of knowledge about the abandoned and forgotten robots by allowing them to live through its' experience and meet other abandoned robots gaining knowledge about them while doing so in a fun way, full of adventure and exploration. This issue is extremely important as in our age there are 3 times more kids who want to become YouTubers than astronauts. Thus, by informing them in a fun way about the unknown and forgotten space robots we are creating more passion and knowledge in our young generation in this ever important space age.
details: The game is an abandoned robot's adventure through Mars, Mercury and the Moon. There are controls in the form of the arrow keys or WADS or on mobile there is a joystick and W. The benefits of the game are that its both web and mobile, and that upon competing it the player can write their name and receive a completion certificate they can download. This can be useful for teachers as they encourage to play it in class. In terms of tools we used Claude Code to build the website, connecting it to Vercel.app. The design was also built through Claude Code. The video game and the details within it (mission, chests, robots) are original to us. The pitch deck was also built with Claude Code. We also used it to gather research and as well as the links provided by the NASA Challenge. Then we used screen record and CapCut to record and edit the demo. Ultimately, we used Canva to perfect the pitch deck.
